item.title: Memories of Storm Éowyn impact on West Cavan
item.description: A West Cavan man has been remembering Storm Éowyn as we approach the first anniversary of the weather event. Storm Éowyn made landfall on January 24th 2025 and was the one of the most powerful and widespread wind events to hit Ireland. As the first anniversary approaches local people have been reflecting on the fallout of it, as well as the community spirit that was shown after and the lessons that can be learned for future events. item.title: Cavan based man describes dog attack
item.description: A Co. Cavan based man has outlined his experiences of being attacked by a dog. Gerard Smith was out walking after Christmas when he was bitten by a dog. Speaking on the Joe Finnegan Show this morning, Gerard outlined his experiences with the dog. Advertisement He said that there was something in the way looked at him that let him know he was "in trouble." Gerard explained how he reacted the incident. item.title: Monaghan resident further charged over alleged human trafficking
item.description: A 57 year old Latvian national who was refused High Court bail on suspicion of human trafficking a woman into the country for the purpose of exploitation has been served with two further charges. Dainis Grinfelds, with an address at Dublin Street, Monaghan town, was brought before a sitting of Monaghan District Court where details surrounding both charges were brought before Judge Raymond Finnegan. item.description: A Co Cavan councillor is calling for Larry Murrin, chairperson of Bord Bia to resign. Bord Bia has responsibility for promoting Irish food, drink and agriculture abroad. According to Cllr Shane P O'Reilly, Mr Murrin is the Chief Executive Officer of Dawn Farm Foods which were proven to have used Brazilian beef in their products. item.title: Mercosur deferral a 'victory for farmers' says Mullooly
item.description: Midlands-North-West MEP Ciaran Mullooly has welcomed today's decision by the European Parliament to refer the EU-Mercosur trade agreement to the European Court. He described the vote as a pivotal moment for legal certainty, democratic oversight, and the protection of European farmers. item.title: Water drainage on roads a major concern across Ballybay/Clones
item.description: Local land and property owners dealing with drainage issues are being encouraged to contact Monaghan County Council to avoid being held responsible for any potential road traffic incidents. Cllr Sean Gilliland said serious issues with drainage on roads across the Ballybay and Clones area was "evident" during the recent cold spell.
